messages:
michelle: Heads up — planning to run accounts schema change tonight in the 00:30 UTC change window. This is an ONLINE ALTER + batched backfill for email_normalized (nullable -> not null) and a small partial index. Need: lock freeze at 00:25, canary on tenant shards, and a pinned API rollout for the window. @db-admin can you confirm lock strategy and estimated exclusive time? @pavan will pin API versions?

db-admin: Got it. We can do an online alter using pg_repack pattern to avoid long exclusive locks for the index. The NOT NULL backfill will be batched: loop of
```sql
UPDATE accounts SET email_normalized = lower(email) WHERE email_normalized IS NULL AND id > $last_id LIMIT 10000;
```
Estimate: ~8-12m per full-tenant run for avg tenant (2M rows total across all tenants we touch). Exclusive lock only briefly for final constraint add (~10-20s). We'll set statement_timeout=10m for backfill jobs and monitor.

pavan: I will pin API to v3.4.2-canary for the 5% shard canary, then promote to v3.4.2 if green. I'll add a rollout hold so we can abort quickly. Also adding feature-flag guard to keep write paths tolerant of nullable checks.

michelle: Canary plan: apply migration on 3 shard groups (5% traffic) at 00:10 UTC, run backfill there, validate for 20m. If OK, rollout remaining shards at 00:30 window. Rollback criteria: any of these triggers rollback -> 1) replica lag > 5s for 5m, 2) 99p latency spike > 300ms for 5m, 3) failed backfill job > 10% errors.

ryan: Oncall will set alerts. I'll add temporary pager rule for DB lock_wait > 200ms sustained 3m and replica lag > 5s. If triggered, we'll pause rollout and follow abort. Also adding a metric for backfill error rate.

michelle: Rollback path: deploy-bot will run schema-revert job which applies the reverse constraint (drop constraint + revert default) and run the revert migration. We should not rely on full restore unless we hit data corruption. We'll also unpin API and rollback to previous stable rollout. Put the exact rollback commands in the runbook.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: queued migration job mjob-206000-A on prod-db-1 (canary). Logs: https://ci.redwood.example/mjob-206000-A. Canary start scheduled 2060001600.

db-admin: For progress visibility we'll upsert a sentinel row in migration_progress table after each batch:
```sql
INSERT INTO migration_progress (migration, shard, last_id) VALUES ('accounts-email-nn', 'shard-17', $last_id) ON CONFLICT (migration, shard) DO UPDATE SET last_id = EXCLUDED.last_id;
```
This lets us resume safely if we abort.

michelle: Good. Make sure the runbook includes the exact psql commands and the revert script name (revert_accounts_email_nn.sql). Also include the exact feature-flag toggle steps for API pin.

pavan: Pin command:
```bash
kubectl set image deploy/api api=registry/redwood/api:v3.4.2-canary --record
# then rollout pause
kubectl rollout pause deploy/api
```
I'll add the rollout annotation to link to this thread.

ryan: I'll be watching the following dashboards during the window: db.locks.wait_time, db.replica.lag, api.request.latency. I added a 15m runbook action: if any alert fires, call this thread and escalate to infra-1.

michelle: I'll post a "going" 15m before and a final confirmation 5m before the canary. After canary is green we'll proceed to window. If all clear, we expect full apply finished by ~00:55 UTC.

db-admin: One more: we'll throttle backfill concurrency to 4 workers per shard to keep replica lag low. If we see lag > 3s we'll drop to 2 workers.

pavan: Acked. I'll hold the rollout and be ready to unpin.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary started (mjob-206000-A) at 2060001600. Logs streaming at https://ci.redwood.example/mjob-206000-A/stream

michelle: Thanks all — will update here with real times. :thumbsup:
